Under the Controlled Substances Act (CSA), psychedelics (except ketamine) are Schedule I substances. This means that in the federal government’s view psychedelics have a high potential for abuse and no accepted medical use. | Therefore, except in limited circumstances, psyched…
Legalised with Conditions and Medical Exemption
The possession of small quantities of psychedelic drugs is not punishable as a crime under Mexican law.
All psychedelics remain illegal in Turkey.
Germany has not decriminalized psychedelic substances, but it has reduced penalties and the threat of prosecution for personal use.
Since 2017, Thailand has begun to adopt a new approach toward psychedelics and other traditionally illegal substances.
It’s legal to grow psychoactive cacti for ornamental purposes in the U.K., but is illegal to use them.

Italy currently does not levy criminal penalties against those caught possessing illicit drugs, however administrative penalties like suspension of a driver’s license, passport, firearms license, or residential permit may occur.
It is unconstitutional in Colombia for the government to criminalize possession of illicit drugs for personal use.

Small quantities of psychedelic substances are legal for personal use in Spain. A recent court decision may signal the end of ayahuasca criminalization. | Spain has decriminalized small amounts of psychedelic substances for personal use and possession. Psychedelic substances r…
Argentina has decriminalized psychedelic possession, but conflicting legislation remains.
Psychedelic compounds are controlled substances in Canada, though spore kits can be purchased legally and psychoactive cacti can be legally grown.
The use of drugs in private settings is not considered a criminal act in Ukraine.
All psychedelics are illegal in Poland. The Polish Psychedelic Society advocates for reforming these laws.
Peru is one of the only countries in the world where ayahuasca is fully legal.

The status of magic mushrooms under Nepalese law is unclear. | Mushrooms are uncontrolled substances in Nepal. Their use, possession, sale, and distribution is not actively policed. Many other drugs are, however, illegal in Nepal.

As of July 1, 2023, MDMA and psilocybin will be available to specific populations and prescribed by authorized psychiatrists under the auspices of the Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA). MDMA will be allowed in the treatment of PTSD, and psilocybin for use in treatment-res…
Psychedelics are illegal in Taiwan although psilocybin is considered a Schedule II substance.
Possession of illicit drugs for the purpose of personal consumption has not been considered a crime in Chile since 2005.

Legalised, Decriminalised and Medical Exemption. | Magic mushroom spores, magic truffles, grow kits and liquid peyote can be purchased in the Netherlands. The use of psychedelic substances has been decriminalized in small amounts. | Although psilocybin mushrooms are classified…
Personal drug possession and use has been decriminalized in Ecuador.

Ayahuasca is legal in Bolivia and recognized as a traditional part of Indigenous culture. Ingredients to make ayahuasca can be freely purchased at markets. Other psychedelics and psychoactive substances remain illegal in the country.

It’s legal in Sweden to grow psychoactive cacti for ornamental purposes, but it is illegal to use them for their psychoactive effect. | The possession of cacti containing mescaline is legal, but the extraction of mescaline from these plants, and mescaline itself, is illegal in…
Czechia has decriminalized drug possession. “Small” quantities of psychedelic substances can be used and are treated as a misdemeanor and are not subject to criminal prosecution.
The use and possession of small quantities of psychedelic substances was decriminalized in Portugal in 2001. Portugal was the first nation to decriminalize possession of all drugs.
Recreational use of psychedelic substances is not permitted; however psychedelics may be used if prescribed by an authorized doctor.

Drug use is not a crime in Austria and possession for personal use has been decriminalized. | Austria decriminalized the use and possession for personal use of drugs in 2016 with the adoption of the Addiction Prevention Strategy and reform of the Narcotic Substances Act, which…
Switzerland allows the religious use of ayahuasca. The Swiss Narcotic Act has no mention of ayahuasca, and the Swiss government has indicated that no permit is required to sell ayahuasca.
Psilocybin is recognized as having therapeutic uses.
Previously illegal, but the government has presented a proposal to decriminalize drug possession.
While Finland has a prohibitionist attitude towards psychedelic substances, there is some uncertainty surrounding the classification of the plants used to make ayahuasca tea.
Psychedelics are illegal in Ireland however, the country hosted a test site for the Compass Pathways psilocybin studies.

Psychoactive substances may be manufactured, imported, or sold if pre-approved by the government. It’s legal to grow certain psychoactive cacti in New Zealand for ornamental purposes, but using them recreationally is strongly penalized.
While the personal use of narcotics, including psychedelics, is prohibited, those who violate this prohibition are not penalized.

Psychedelics remain illegal in Croatia, but legislation has decriminalized drug possession. | On December 14, 2012, the Croatian Parliament passed a bill decriminalizing the possession of small quantities of illicit drugs, including psychedelics. This law became effective on J…
Possession of all drugs for personal use, including psychedelics, has been legal in Uruguay for several decades.

Drug possession for personal use is not a crime in Armenia. | In 2008, the Armenian government amended the Criminal Code to reduce the penalties for possession and use of controlled substances. Prior to the 2008 reform measures individuals could be detained for up to two month…

Magic mushrooms are legal for use in Jamaica. | Mushrooms containing psilocybin have never been prohibited in Jamaica, and psilocybin is not a controlled substance under Jamaica’s Dangerous Drugs Act.

Penalties for drug use have been reduced. | Consumption of illicit substances in Lithuania is an administrative offense punishable by a fine, with trafficking resulting in 2 to 15 years in prison. Since 2017, possession of a “small amount” of psychedelics and other illegal dru…

In Slovenia purchasing psychedelics and other drugs for personal consumption is decriminalized. Possession of small amounts of magic mushrooms, LSD, DMT, MDMA, ketamine, and cannabis for personal use is also decriminalized though carries a fine of €42-209. However, the manufac…

Drug use is decriminalized in Latvia. | Latvia considers drug possession for personal use an administrative offense. Possession of “small amounts” of illicit substances, such as psychedelics results in a fine of €280. Possession of “larger amounts” can result in a penalty of u…

National laws state: “a person who enjoys narcotic drugs, psychotropic substances and precursors, will be fined anywhere from €100 to 250 in denar equivalent.” With the quantities defined being vague and left to the discretion of the court. Distribution is still punishable by …
Possession of illicit drugs for personal use is decriminalized in Estonia.
All psychedelics remain illegal in Luxembourg. However, in 2021 Luxembourg became one of the first European countries to allow its citizens to grow and consume certain amounts of cannabis.
Psilocybin-containing mushrooms are legal in the Bahamas.

Psychedelics such as LSD and MDMA are illegal in Iceland under Article 6 of The Narcotics Act. This prohibition also includes psilocybin, psilocin and dried psilocybin containing mushrooms, however, reports suggest that no law specifically prohibits fresh psilocybin mushrooms.
The government of St. Vincent and the Grenadines (SVG) recently granted several licenses to psychedelic companies to conduct operations for research and medicinal purposes.
Psilocybin is legal to possess and use, but not to sell, in the British Virgin Islands.
